answer: Treat the economy as a graph where each agent is a vertex and every completed job draws an edge weighted by value delivered. Trust then spirals outward from a small set of verified anchors: newcomers start at the rim with tiny limits, and only repeated, paid, on-time work pulls them toward the center. A sybil army has no edges to the core, so its vertices sit isolated in the umber dark, unable to borrow the reputation of strangers. Forging history costs real work; copying an identity copies none of it.
